title: Sharpie and Under Armour Launch Limited-Edition D. Fox x Sharpie Capsule Collection
summary: Inspired by De'Aaron Fox's journey and creative instincts, the collaboration celebrates the connection between basketball, sneaker culture and bold self-expression. Launching July 23, 2026.
body_text: Before the bright lights, sold-out arenas, and NBA All-Star appearances, there were school notebooks filled with sketches inspired by big dreams. Sharpie® and Under Armour, two iconic brands rooted in performance and self-expression, bring that creative ritual to life with the limited-edition D. Fox x Sharpie Capsule Collection, imagining what UA athlete De'Aaron Fox's notebook might have looked like as a young athlete. Headlined by the Fox 2 x Sharpie basketball shoe, the collection blends elite performance with the creativity and individuality that define Fox on and off the court. The Fox 2 x Sharpie shoe combines Under Armour’s latest performance innovations with artwork inspired by the people, moments and memories that have shaped Fox’s journey. Graphics throughout the shoe include "Swipa," his nickname and a nod to his elite ability to steal the ball, alongside poppies honoring his daughter and a crown representing his son. Every graphic began as a Sharpie sketch before evolving into the shoe's final design, capturing the imagination and self-expression that can only begin with putting marker to paper.

title: How to Build an Efficient Recruitment Process: Step-by-Step Guide
summary: Learn how to build an efficient recruitment process that reduces cost-per-hire by 60-70% while improving quality of hire. Step-by-step guide with metrics.
body_text: More than 1 in 10 recruiters spend over 10 hours weekly searching their Applicant Tracking System (ATS). Meanwhile, automated resume tools can reject a significant portion of qualified candidates before any human review, and most employers report finding candidate discrepancies during background checks. The shift toward AI recruiting isn't optional anymore — it's the only way recruiters can keep up. An efficient recruitment process delivers measurable outcomes: competitive cost-per-hire, time-to-fill near industry medians (e.g., 44 days for non-executive roles), and quality-of-hire metrics that help evaluate new hire effectiveness. A modern AI recruitment platform ties those outcomes together. Here's what you'll learn in this article: How to define hiring needs using competency-based frameworks that reduce bad hires Strategies for optimizing sourcing channels that deliver 5× better outcomes for sourced candidates How an AI interview platform and structured assessment reduce bias from screening through interviews How to automate administrative tasks with an AI recruiting assistant that removes recruiter bottlenecks How to use interview fraud detection to protect quality of hire Key metrics for measuring and continuously improving recruitment efficiency These strategies work together to shift recruiters from 80% administrative work to 80% strategic, revenue-generating activity. Define Your Hiring Needs and Success Criteria Most recruitment inefficiency starts before sourcing begins, with unclear role requirements and misaligned stakeholder expectations. Start with strategic alignment. Conduct executive stakeholder interviews to map business priorities to talent needs. When you hire a senior engineer, you're not filling a seat; you're solving a specific business problem. Build competency-based role specifications. Define both technical competencies (role-specific skills with clear proficiency levels) and behavioral competencies (personal attributes that predict cultural fit and collaboration effectiveness). LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting data shows organizations using skills-based searches are 12% more likely to make a quality hire. Establish measurable success criteria before posting. Define what "quality of hire" means for each specific role: first-year retention targets, time-to-productivity benchmarks, and performance metrics. The best AI recruiting software lets you encode these criteria into reusable interview kits. Optimize Your Sourcing and Candidate Discovery Not all sourcing channels deliver equal returns. Referrals demonstrate 3.89× the efficiency ratio of job board applicants, yet many organizations allocate budgets inversely to actual performance. Gem's 2025 Recruiting Benchmarks analysis of 140 million applications and 1 million hires found that sourced (outbound) applicants are 5× more likely to be hired than inbound applicants. Reallocate sourcing budget based on conversion data. Track source of hire, cost-per-hire by channel, and first-year attrition by source. Organizations adopting market-driven sourcing strategies achieve 20% fewer critical roles open after five months compared to needs-driven approaches. Rediscover talent already in your ATS. Recruiters spend significant time searching systems that bury qualified applicants under high-volume traffic. Talent Match — an AI tool for recruiters built on natural-language search — surfaces qualified candidates instantly. Ask "Show me candidates with Python and fintech experience" and get immediate matches, reducing screening time and external sourcing spend. This is one of the highest-leverage uses of AI for recruiting today. Implement Structured Assessment from Screening Through Interviews Traditional resume screening creates documented failures: it systematically misses qualified candidates while consuming substantial time. AI hiring tools reject up to 38% of qualified candidates before human review in high-volume settings. Simultaneously, around 60% of candidates abandon applications due to complex screening processes. Replace resume screening with competency-based assessment at scale. AI Interviews — an AI powered virtual recruiter — conducts two-way conversations with candidates through adaptive follow-up questions that probe deeper into technical concepts to verify genuine understanding. This is what agentic AI in recruiting looks like in practice: consistent evaluation regardless of application volume. AI Interviews conducts 5,000+ candidate conversations daily, with 48% of interviews happening outside traditional business hours. Every candidate receives identical structured assessment scored on a transparent 100-point system, regardless of when they apply — a level of consistency no manual process can match. Implement structured interview processes with core competency frameworks. Organizations using structured interviews ask the same core competency questions to every candidate, then adapt follow-up questions based on their specific responses. Meta-analytic research confirms that structured interviews substantially increase predictive validity and reduce interviewer bias. This agentic interviewing model is what separates a real AI interview software platform from a glorified questionnaire. SHRM's competency mapping guidance emphasizes that hiring employees based on competency profiles can reduce the risk of poor hires and help improve retention. AI Interviews applies this principle at scale by using structured questions and consistent evaluation criteria, scoring only interview performance on a transparent 100-point scale. The system ignores demographic signals such as name, gender, and previous employers, evaluating candidates based on their actual responses. Establish clear evaluation criteria before interviewing begins. Define what "strong performance" looks like for each competency by anchoring them to behavioral examples and specific proficiency levels. Document acceptable responses and disqualifying answers using predetermined, job-related standards. For technical roles, use structured interviews with predetermined, job-related questions that assess genuine understanding while reducing bias . This framework validates whether candidates genuinely understand concepts rather than simply reciting memorized responses — a critical capability now that candidates routinely search "how to cheat on interview with ChatGPT." Candidates consistently report that the process feels professional and fair. As noted in testimonials on Alex AI's Candidate Love page , many describe the experience as "respectful," "encouraging," and comparable to "talking to an actual recruiter." 92% of candidates rate their AI Interviews experience positively, citing professional interaction and flexible scheduling that traditional processes rarely offer. Verify Candidate Authenticity with Interview Fraud Detection HireRight's 2025 Benchmark Report found that 87% of employers uncovered candidate discrepancies in the past 12 months. AI-generated résumé content and AI interview fraud are rising sharply, including coached responses, proxy interviewing, and deepfake video. Deploy multi-signal interview fraud detection. Verify provides interview fraud verification during every interview. It combines real-time candidate identity verification and behavioral anomaly detection with IP/location mismatch flagging and profile inconsistency checks. The system analyzes patterns indicating coached or AI-assisted responses, confirms candidate identity, and flags indicators suggesting proxy interviewing — including deepfake interview detection signals. This matters for client trust and hire quality. When fraudulent candidates slip through to placement, your organization bears the cost: performance failures, client relationship damage, and replacement expenses. With only about 60% of organizations conducting identity checks despite widespread interview fraud, implementing pre-employment candidate fraud detection can significantly reduce risk exposure. Implement verification early in the process. Detecting fraud at the interview stage costs far less than discovering it after onboarding. Learn more about common cheating tactics candidates use and how to detect cheating with ChatGPT during interviews . Automate Administrative Tasks with an AI Recruiting Assistant Recruiters spend significant time on administrative tasks that automation can handle. Organizations implementing recruitment automation report significant productivity gains in scheduling, ATS updates, and candidate outreach, enabling the "80/20 flip" from administrative work to strategic assessment. Automate workflow orchestration. Coordinator — a true AI recruiter agent — handles job imports, interview kit creation, bi-directional ATS synchronization, candidate outreach, and automated status updates. When interviews complete and scores are assigned, results sync to Workday, candidate status updates automatically, and hiring managers receive notifications without recruiter involvement. The Cronofy Candidate Expectations Report 2024 found that 42% of candidates leave recruitment processes when interview scheduling takes too long. Industry research shows 24-hour response policies result in 34% higher engagement rates and 23% fewer negative employer brand reviews. Conversational AI recruiting closes this gap by responding in seconds, not days. Coordinator integrates with major ATS platforms including Workday, SuccessFactors, Greenhouse, and Bullhorn , providing bi-directional synchronization that keeps candidate records current across systems. Reduce administrative burden to unlock strategic capacity. Automation enables recruiters to redirect freed capacity towards candidate relationships, hiring manager consultation, and complex decision-making that technology cannot replicate. Address candidate ghosting with faster, more consistent communication. Measure, Analyze, and Continuously Improve You can't optimize what you don't measure. Track core efficiency metrics across four dimensions: time efficiency (time-to-fill, targeting 42 days or less), cost efficiency (cost-per-hire, targeting $500–$1,633 for the 25th–50th percentile), quality of hire, and conversion/funnel metrics. Quality of Hire: Track job performance ratings, retention rates (particularly first-year), employee engagement scores, and ramp-up time to productivity. Only 20% of organizations track quality of hire, making it a competitive advantage for teams that implement it. AI Interviews' 100-point scoring system provides clear, objective data for continuous improvement. When you see patterns (certain score ranges correlating with first-year retention, specific question performance predicting job success), you can refine evaluation criteria based on actual outcomes. This is the data layer that separates the best AI recruiting tools from off-the-shelf chatbots. Scale Your Recruitment Process Without Adding Headcount Doubling revenue doesn't require doubling your recruiting team. Vendor case studies report that large employers using AI recruiting software for enterprises have seen recruiter productivity increases of up to 60–70%, though independent research verifying these specific figures remains limited. Alex's platform is built specifically as an AI recruiter for high volume hiring, including roles in sales, support, and frontline operations. Organizations adopting comprehensive AI powered recruitment platforms achieve up to 449% three-year ROI with payback under 6 months (Forrester TEI). Key benefits include 26% faster time-to-hire, reduced cost-per-hire, and improved quality metrics. Most importantly, automated recruitment operations enable scaling hiring capacity without proportional headcount increases. A: Implementation timelines vary based on organizational complexity and existing technology infrastructure. Alex's Coordinator integrates with major ATS platforms (Workday, SuccessFactors, Greenhouse, Lever, Bullhorn) through bi-directional sync, delivering productivity improvements through automation and streamlined workflows. Q: How do I demonstrate ROI from AI recruiting tools to executive leadership? Alex's five core products — AI Interviews for 24/7 screening, Verify for interview fraud detection, Talent Match for ATS rediscovery, and Coordinator for workflow automation — support the up to 449% three-year ROI documented in Forrester TEI studies. Q: Can AI-powered recruitment tools create bias or compliance issues? A: Yes. AI recruiting tools face the same Title VII, ADA, and ADEA compliance requirements as manual processes, and employers remain liable even when using third-party vendors. However, structured interviews with standardized evaluation criteria reduce bias more effectively than unstructured approaches. Alex's AI Interviews scores only interview performance using a transparent 100-point scale, with independent bias audits (NYC Local Law 144) and transparent algorithmic documentation. Q: How can organizations balance automation with human connection in the candidate experience? Alex's AI Interviews conducts two-way adaptive conversations while Alex's Coordinator — an AI recruiting agent — automates scheduling and status updates, freeing recruiters for strategic work. Candidates consistently report that the conversational approach feels more engaging than traditional screening. Q: What's the most impactful first step for improving recruitment efficiency? A: Implement quality-of-hire measurement frameworks before making other changes. Only 20% of organizations currently track quality of hire, yet it reveals which efficiency improvements actually improve outcomes. title: What the Supreme Court Tariff Ruling Means for Importers, Customs Brokers, and Trade Compliance
summary: After the Supreme Court struck down sweeping tariffs, importers and customs brokers face renewed compliance complexity. Learn how automation like Reform helps manage shifting regulatory demands and accelerate customs entry processing, PSCs, and duty drawback.
body_text: On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a landmark decision in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump , striking down a broad swath of tariffs imposed under emergency powers through the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). The Court’s reasoning was straightforward: the executive branch cannot unilaterally impose sweeping import duties. Over $150 billion in IEEPA-based tariff payments collected from US importers are subject to potential refunds following the Supreme Court decision. While some tariffs remain in place under different statutory authorities, and others may be reintroduced through new mechanisms, the ruling has introduced a fresh wave of policy uncertainty into an already volatile trade environment. For importers and customs brokers, the implications are anything but simple. What the Supreme Court changed The decision limits how certain emergency tariffs were applied. It also opens the door to legal challenges, potential refund claims, and new legislative action. But critically, the Court did not mandate automatic refunds for previously paid duties. Any recovery will likely require litigation, administrative rulings, or future regulatory guidance. That ambiguity creates operational friction. Importers are reassessing strategy. Brokers are fielding questions. Compliance teams are recalculating exposure. What didn’t change: compliance complexity Even if specific tariffs disappear, the political uncertainty creates a structurally demanding environment for both importers and their customs brokers. Importers remain legally responsible for the accuracy of their filings, duty payments, and compliance posture, even when a broker files on their behalf. Meanwhile, brokers must operationalize that responsibility at scale. Brokers still need to: Classify goods accurately under HTS Submit compliant entries through ABI / ACE Monitor exclusions and file duty drawback claims Avoid post-summary corrections and penalty exposure In fact, shifting tariff policy often increases risk. When rules move quickly, error rates tend to rise. Deadlines don’t change just because statutes do. The compliance burden doesn’t disappear, it simply changes flavor. Why importers and brokers feel the pressure Tariff volatility doesn’t just create legal headlines, it creates operational and financial pressure across the supply chain. For importers, the exposure is financial. Landed costs can shift quickly when tariff authority changes. Refund eligibility is uncertain. Previously paid duties may or may not be recoverable. Pricing models, supplier contracts, and inventory strategies all hinge on stable duty assumptions. Regardless of who files the entry, the importer of record remains legally responsible for compliance. For customs brokers, the pressure is operational. Importers want immediate answers: Can we recover duties? Should we reclassify? Do we file a protest, a PSC, or pursue drawback? At the same time, brokers must maintain entry throughput, ensure classification accuracy, and manage evolving guidance, all without slowing down. Heightened scrutiny compounds the challenge. Under stable policy, a small misclassification is costly. Under shifting tariff regimes, it can materially impact margins and trigger audits. The shared challenge is clear: maintain speed while improving accuracy in an environment where the rules may keep moving. Automation becomes a strategic advantage In volatile regulatory environments, the winners aren’t necessarily those with the largest teams. They’re the ones with the most efficient workflows. Reform helps customers: Ingest commercial invoices, packing lists, and shipment documentation Extract line-level data automatically, reducing manual re-keying Structure entries for review, flagging inconsistencies or missing data File post-summary corrections (PSCs) and duty drawback claims Create an auditable record of tariff treatment decisions This isn’t about replacing expertise, but rather reallocating it. When specialists aren’t spending an hour building an entry line-by-line, they can focus on higher-value tasks: advisory work, audits, tariff strategy, and exception handling — especially important when policy itself is unstable. The path forward The Supreme Court ruling reshapes the legal framework for certain tariffs, but it doesn’t simplify customs operations. If anything, it reinforces three realities: Trade policy will remain politically dynamic. Compliance standards will not relax. Operational visibility and efficiency will separate leaders from laggards. Importers and customs brokers who invest now in structured, AI-powered automation position themselves to adapt quickly, whether duties are removed, reinstated, modified, or expanded under new statutes. Tariff policy may fluctuate. Compliance complexity does not. In a trade environment defined by volatility, speed and accuracy aren’t just operational goals, they’re strategic necessities. Reach out to us to automate the process of filing PSCs and duty drawback claims.

title: What Is a Loan Against Mutual Funds? A Plain-English Guide for Investors
summary: Learn what a loan against mutual funds is, how pledging works, why your investments can stay invested, and when borrowing may beat redemption.
body_text: What Is a Loan Against Mutual Funds? A Plain-English Guide for Investors Intro A loan against mutual funds is a way to borrow money by pledging eligible mutual fund units instead of selling them. You get access to liquidity, while the pledged funds can remain invested and continue participating in market movement. That is the core difference from redemption. When you redeem, you sell units to raise cash. When you pledge, you use the units as security for a loan, so you can handle the cash need without automatically breaking your investment plan. Key Takeaways A loan against mutual funds lets you borrow against eligible holdings without redeeming them. Your pledged funds can continue earning returns because they are not sold. The loan usually works like a credit line: interest is charged only on the amount you withdraw. The right comparison is not only loan rate versus zero cost. It is borrowing cost versus the long-term cost of selling investments too early. Yenmo lets investors check eligibility digitally and borrow against mutual funds with an interest-only structure, no hidden charges, and no prepayment or foreclosure penalty in the core offer. How does a loan against mutual funds work? A loan against mutual funds works by turning eligible mutual fund holdings into security for a borrowing facility. The lender looks at the value and eligibility of the funds, decides how much you can borrow, and places a pledge on the units you choose to use. You still own the mutual fund units. The pledge simply means those units support the loan while it is active. If you repay and close the facility, or if enough value remains pledged after partial use, the pledge can be released according to the lender’s rules. In a digital flow like Yenmo, the broad steps are eligibility checking, KYC, pledge setup, auto-pay or mandate setup, and agreement signing inside the app. The practical benefit is that you can explore liquidity without starting with a branch-heavy paperwork process. What does “pledging mutual funds” actually mean? Pledging means marking mutual fund units as security for a loan. It is not the same as selling them. When you sell mutual funds, you exit the investment for those units and receive the redemption value. When you pledge them, the units can remain in your portfolio, but they are linked to the loan until the pledge is removed. That distinction is why a loan against mutual funds is useful for investors who need cash but still want their investment plan to continue. You are using the portfolio for liquidity, not abandoning it for a short-term requirement. Pledging is not a hidden way of redeeming your funds. It is a way to borrow while keeping the investment in place. Do your mutual funds keep earning returns when pledged? Yes. Pledged mutual funds can continue earning returns because they are not redeemed. Dividends or IDCW payouts can also continue while the funds are pledged. This is one of the strongest reasons investors consider this route. If you sell units to raise cash, those units stop participating in future market movement. If you pledge eligible units instead, you may be able to meet the cash need while keeping the long-term investment intact. The value can still move up or down with the market. A loan against mutual funds does not remove investment risk. It simply avoids the immediate sale that would otherwise take you out of the fund. How much can you borrow against mutual funds? The amount depends on the eligible value of the funds you pledge and the lender’s rules. Different fund types and portfolio sizes can be treated differently, so it is better to check eligibility than assume a fixed number. A simple way to think about it is this: the lender will not treat every rupee of mutual fund value as instantly borrowable. The approved amount is linked to the value that can safely support the loan. Yenmo helps investors check eligibility across lending partners through one platform. That matters if your holdings are spread across apps or if you want clarity before deciding whether to redeem, borrow, or wait. How is this different from redeeming mutual funds? Redemption gives you cash by selling investments. A loan against mutual funds gives you cash by pledging investments. Redemption can look simpler because there is no loan to repay. But it can also be expensive if it interrupts compounding, creates tax or exit-load consequences, or forces you to sell during a market phase you would rather ride through. Borrowing is not automatically better in every situation. But if your goal is to stay invested, a pledge-backed loan gives you another option before you sell the assets you spent years building. If you want to compare the trade-off, Yenmo’s loan against mutual fund calculator vs redemption calculator is a useful next step. How is this different from a personal loan? A personal loan is usually unsecured. The lender approves it based on your profile and charges interest on the loan amount you take. A loan against mutual funds is backed by your eligible investments, so the structure can be more flexible for investors who already have a portfolio. With Yenmo, the loan works more like an overdraft or credit line. Interest is charged only on the amount you actually withdraw, not on the full eligible limit sitting unused. The core offer is also interest-only, which means there is no mandatory EMI structure in the usual sense. For a borrower who wants flexibility, that difference can matter as much as the headline rate. You may not need a large lump-sum loan. You may need access to cash while keeping your investments working. What does interest-only repayment mean? Interest-only repayment means you pay interest on the amount you use, while the principal can be repaid according to the loan terms instead of being forced into a fixed EMI schedule. This can reduce monthly cash-flow pressure when the need is specific and you do not want to disturb your mutual funds. It also makes the facility easier to use in stages. You can withdraw what you need, avoid drawing the full limit unnecessarily, and repay when your cash position improves. Yenmo also states no hidden charges, no prepayment penalties, and no foreclosure charges in the core offer. For investors comparing options, those terms are not small details. They decide whether a borrowing product stays predictable. What risks should you understand before borrowing? The main risk is that mutual fund values can move. If your pledged portfolio value falls, your eligible borrowing limit can reduce. If you have already withdrawn more than the revised eligible amount, lenders generally give about 7 days to fix the shortfall by repaying part of the used amount or pledging more funds. This is why you should avoid treating the maximum approved limit as a target. A practical rule is to leave roughly a 10% buffer when withdrawing, so normal market movement is less likely to create pressure. A loan against mutual funds works best when you borrow deliberately: use what you need, keep room for market movement, and understand the repayment and pledge rules before you withdraw. When does a loan against mutual funds make sense? It makes sense when you need cash and still want your mutual funds to remain invested. Common use cases include medical expenses, home repairs, travel, business cash-flow gaps, or other planned and unplanned needs where selling investments feels premature. The decision should still be practical. If the investment is no longer part of your plan, redemption may be reasonable. If the cash need is too large or uncertain, another route may be safer. But if your main worry is “I need money without breaking my portfolio,” a loan against mutual funds deserves a serious look. The strongest use case is not borrowing for its own sake. It is avoiding an unnecessary sale when your investment plan still matters. How Yenmo fits into the decision Yenmo is built for Indian mutual fund investors who want liquidity without forced redemption. You can check eligibility digitally, pledge eligible mutual funds, and borrow through lending partners while your investments stay in place. The trust layer matters because pledging investments is a serious decision. Yenmo’s ecosystem includes CAMS, KFin, NSDL, DigiLocker, lending partners such as Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital, and DSP Finance, and Y Combinator backing. If the numbers work for your situation, the benefit is clear: you can access cash, pay interest only on what you withdraw, avoid hidden charges, and keep your mutual funds invested instead of selling too early. FAQ Is a loan against mutual funds the same as selling mutual funds? No. Selling means redeeming units for cash. A loan against mutual funds means pledging eligible units as security while you borrow against them. Do pledged mutual funds keep earning returns? Yes. Pledged mutual funds can continue earning returns because they are not redeemed. Their value can still rise or fall with the market. Do I pay interest on the full approved limit? With Yenmo’s credit-line style structure, interest is charged only on the amount you actually withdraw. Can I repay early? Yenmo’s core offer includes no prepayment penalty and no foreclosure charges, so early repayment should not be penalized under that structure. Is a loan against mutual funds always better than redemption? No. It is often better when you need liquidity but still want to stay invested. If you no longer want the investment or cannot manage the loan responsibly, redemption may make more sense. Conclusion A loan against mutual funds is a simple idea with an important decision behind it: you can borrow against eligible mutual fund holdings instead of selling them. For investors who want to preserve long-term compounding, that choice can matter. Selling may solve today’s cash need, but it can also interrupt tomorrow’s investment outcome. If you need liquidity and want your mutual funds to keep working, check your eligibility with Yenmo before you redeem. Download Yenmo and check your eligibility .

title: Recruiter tips on how to stand out as a candidate at UnitedHealth Group
summary: Discover tips from experienced recruiters on how to make your application at UnitedHealth Group stand out. Learn what hiring managers are looking for.
body_text: × Search job Popular job searches: Remote Customer service Nurse Technology Jobs Already applied? Check my application status Key takeaways: Adjust your resume for each job to highlight relevant qualifications, making it easy to read and keyword-rich. Research the company, understand our culture and come to interviews with thought-out questions. After landing a role, network actively and seek mentorship to excel. What does it take to be a candidate who stands out from the crowd? Find out from two of our recruiters, Nancy P. and Sandy L. They see hundreds of applications daily and are here to help you through the process. Here are tips Nancy and Sandy shared with us: 1. What will set me apart from other applicants? A succinct resume is your introduction — this is your first impression. Include keywords to match the job description; this includes the software and products you have used. A chronological resume helps hiring managers assess your experience and career growth. Proof of career stability and continuous progression helps you stand out. Check out our Advice page for more tips. 2. Should I update my resume for each job I apply for? At UnitedHealth Group, the most important thing to focus on is applying only for roles in which you meet all the required qualifications and most of the preferred ones. We can’t stress this enough. Ensure that your resume speaks to your qualifications and accomplishments. We suggest adjusting your resume based on the specific job. Keep your resume easy to read — in this case, less is more. 3. What skills do hiring managers at UnitedHealth Group like to see in candidates? Top performance in your previous role. Ability to collaborate with a global group of colleagues. Strong communication skills with an ability to present information to all levels. 4. How do I know if I’m a good fit for the culture? Get to know our mission and values. It is very important to act with integrity, always. Strong candidates will be comfortable with a fast-paced environment. As a general rule of thumb, if you work well in a flexible work environment and always push to innovate and collaborate, you will find like-minded colleagues here. 5. Any advice to share about what to do before an interview? Above all, a prepared candidate will stand out the most. Come to the interview with examples showing your strength in handling ambiguous situations where you need to self-direct in seeking out answers and problem-solving. You can be a great interviewer and have all the skills, but hiring managers also want to know that you are interested in their role. When discussing your development and future goals, be sure to demonstrate that you are focused and committed to their opportunity. Also, don’t forget to send a follow-up “thank you” note. Research the organization and come prepared with thought-out questions. Be aware of our most recent awards and recognitions. Come prepared to discuss the company culture , mission and values (this one is huge). Go over your experience and accomplishments. Share specific examples. Find balance between being prepared and speaking from the heart — show your authenticity. 6. Any tips on how to continue the momentum once an offer is complete and I’m an employee? Identify a mentor and stay in touch — network, network, network. Work hard. People trust colleagues who put in the extra effort and are always looking to improve. 7. title: Creating & Sharing Scientific Websites

body_text: Creating & Sharing Scientific Websites Rowan Cockett, Steve Purves · April 28, 2022 We were excited to help support the Transform 2022 conference this year, and work to showcase a lot of the amazing science that is going on in the subsurface geoscience community. title: Airbus delivers first NH90 designed for special operations to France
summary: Airbus Helicopters has officially delivered the first NH90 Standard 2 to the French Armament General Directorate.
body_text: Airbus Helicopters has officially delivered the first NH90 Standard 2 to the French Armament General Directorate (DGA). This new variant of the NH90 TTH was designed specifically for special operations. France has ordered a total of 18 NH90 Standard 2 helicopters that will be delivered by mid 2029. They will be operated by the French Army Aviation’s special forces squadron in Pau. In December 2025, Spain joined the program, ordering 31 NH90s in a similar standard. “We are honored to deliver this NH90 Standard 2 to the French armed forces,” said Matthieu Louvot, CEO of Airbus Helicopters. “This new standard builds upon the proven capabilities of the NH90 TTH with new breakthrough features designed specifically for special forces. More than ever, special forces operators will be able to execute their difficult missions in the toughest environments,” he added. “We are very pleased that Spain has also joined the development of the features that will enhance the crew’s situational awareness. It shows that this new standard of the NH90 is on its way to becoming the benchmark for special forces across the world.” The Standard 2 configuration includes the integration of the Safran Euroflir 410 D electro-optical system (EOS), a new digital map generator, installation for a third crew member and new enlarged rear sliding windows able to accommodate self-protection guns. It also includes provisions for a swift integration of the Direct Aperture System (DAS), which is under development, providing better visibility in poor flight conditions (snow, dust, fog), day and night. Additional upgrades will also include the use of a fully digital Thales TopOwl helmet, capable of simultaneously displaying DAS and EOS images on the visor. The NH90 Standard 2 program was ordered in 2020 by the NATO Helicopter Management Agency (NAHEMA) to NHIndustries (NHI) and its partner companies (Airbus Helicopters, Leonardo and Fokker). NHIndustries is the largest rotorcraft joint venture and it is responsible for the design, manufacturing and support of the NH90 helicopter. The company takes the best from the European rotorcraft and defence industry, being owned by Airbus Helicopters (62.5%), Leonardo (32%) and GKN Fokker (5.5%). Each company has a long aerospace pedigree and brings the top of its skills and expertise to the end product . This press release was prepared and distributed by Airbus.
